subject: Token emission SLA: streaming vs sync — waiver request
messages:
From: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@helixretail.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@helixretail.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token emission SLA: streaming vs sync — waiver request

Karthik,

Quick follow-up from our platform team after the pilot run last week. We saw that the streaming endpoint delivers the first token much faster for short responses, but the sustained tokens/sec drops under our expected profile during catalog-sync bursts. Specifically:

- Median time-to-first-token for streaming: ~90ms (good)
- Sustained tokens/sec for our bursts (90s windows): ~1,800 TPS (we expected ~3k)

We understand that streaming and synchronous endpoints have different delivery semantics, but our SREs need an exception or an explicit SLA carve-out for the streaming endpoint for the next 3 months while we iterate on request shaping. Can Redwood grant a temporary waiver for the streaming TTFT commitment and a modified tokens/sec expectation during our ramp?

I attached a small CSV with the request shape we saw. Happy to jump on a short call.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering — HelixRetail
Attachments: traffic_shape_q2.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@helixretail.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@helixretail.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token emission SLA: streaming vs sync — waiver request

Tom — thanks for the note and the sample traffic. Short answer: yes, we can propose a temporary carve-out, but we need to align on measurable commitments and an expiry.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick troubleshooting call with our SREs to review the CSV and confirm if request fanout or tokenization is driving the drop (30 min).
2) Draft a 12-week waiver that relaxes the sustained tokens/sec expectation for streaming endpoints from 3,000 -> 1,800 for burst windows >60s, with a requirement for you to share telemetry and a remediation plan.
3) If agreed, we’ll route the waiver through our Contracts and Security teams for sign-off; target: internal approval within 4 business days.

Jonas from SRE will chime in with the constraints we see and an initial mitigation path. Lauren — assigning for commercial approval of the temporary credit and expiration.

Would Thursday 10am PT work for the call?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@helixretail.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@helixretail.com>, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token emission SLA: streaming vs sync — waiver request

On Thu, May 16, 2028 at 09:12 AM Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@helixretail.com> wrote:
> Karthik,
>
> Quick follow-up from our platform team after the pilot run last week...

Thanks for the clear data, Tom. A few operational notes from SRE after a first-pass review of the CSV:

- Root cause candidate: request cardinality + tokenizer variance. Your catalog requests have a high-entropy payload that expands during tokenization, which increases per-request token work and can lower overall tokens/sec under continuous-batching heuristics.
- Streaming TTFT behavior: for short completions our runtime generally achieves sub-120ms median TTFT on NVIDIA A100 equivalent hosts for <64-token responses. Longer context and tokenizer expansion increases TTFT variance.
- Sustained throughput: our autoscaler and batching scheduler aim for an optimal batch size; however, when many concurrent short requests arrive (your burst pattern), the scheduler trades off latency for batching efficiency which can reduce tokens/sec in short windows.

Operational compromise we can offer (temporary carve-out):
1) Waiver window: 12 weeks from sign-off.
2) Metrics under waiver: streaming TTFT SLA relaxed to p50 < 200ms (instead of p50 < 120ms) for streams with expected response length <= 128 tokens; tokens/sec expectation for 60–120s bursts relaxed to p50 >= 1,750 TPS.
3) Instrumentation: Helix must share an agreed telemetry feed (sampled traces + token counts per request) to INF-3421 so we can track progress.
4) Remediation gates: weekly checkpoints; if tokens/sec does not improve by 20% after week 6, we will require a joint mitigation plan (request shaping, tokenizer harmonization, or model variant change).

Attachment: small repro notes attached inline and a pointer to an internal runbook.

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@helixretail.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@helixretail.com>, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token emission SLA: streaming vs sync — waiver request

Karthik / Jonas — approved in principle.

Commercial terms we will include in the waiver doc: 12-week term, one-time service credit of 5% of the month-to-month hosted spend for the period, and requirement that Helix provide telemetry as Jonas specified. Waiver will expire automatically on 2028-08-03 unless both parties agree to extend.

Tom / Sara — I’ll have Contracts prepare the waiver PDF and route for signatures; the waiver will reference INF-3421 and include the metrics/weekly checkpoint schedule. Please confirm you can provide the telemetry stream and a primary contact for weekly checkpoints.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial — Redwood Inference
